summary: Henrik Zilliacus was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1926 to 1936 and later held a post there from circa 1944 to 1974.

Henry Beveridge worked in history/archaeology and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow and Queen's University Belfast. Professionally, he served in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and was President of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

Henry Chung-hung Shiu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto in 2006, having studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

Henry Clarke Warren was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, under teachers including Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and T. W. Rhys Davids. He founded the Harvard Oriental Series in 1891.

Henry Creswicke Rawlinson worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, later serving in the East India Company (c. 1827–1858), the Foreign Office (c. 1859–1860), and the University of London.

Henry George Keene was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College. He held posts with the East India Company, Sidney Sussex College, and the East India Company College (1824–1834).

Henry Hamilton Hadley specialized in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Yale, Union Theological Seminary, and Andover. He later held posts at Union Theological Seminary and Yale Divinity School as an instructor and professor of Hebrew.

Henry Herbert Dodwell was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied at St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History at SOAS University of London (1922–1946).

Henry Hoenigswald was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the universities of Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence. He served on the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1948 to 1985.
Henry Martyn was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Truro Cathedral School and St John's College, and he studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1804–1805.
Henry Miers Elliot was a scholar in history/archaeology and Indology. He studied at Winchester College and worked as a civil servant for the East India Company from circa 1827 to 1853.
Henry Pitts Forster worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the East India Company and the Bengal Civil Service from 1783 to 1815, and he was Master of the Calcutta Mint from 1803 to 1804.
Henry Steel Olcott was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who attended Columbia University. In 1875, he founded the Theosophical Society.
Henry Sullivan Jarrett was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners at Fort William from circa 1870 to 1892.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He served the East India Company, Bengal Civil Service, and Fort William College, and later became Director of the Royal Asiatic Society and President of the Royal Astronomical Society.
Heramba Chandra Chackravarty is an Indologist who studied under Manindra Mohan Bose. He served as a lecturer at City College, Kolkata, attested in 1977.

Herbert Cushing Tolman worked in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Yale and several other colleges, later holding posts at Yale, Wisconsin-Madison, North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Vanderbilt University (1894–1923).

Herbert Franke was a sinologist and Central Asian scholar. He studied at Cologne, Bonn, Berlin, and under Erich Haenisch. He held posts at Cologne, Munich (1952–1979), and served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Herbert Hope Risley was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his education at Winchester College from circa 1863 to 1869 and at New College from circa 1869 to 1873.

Herbert Härtel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen. He served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (1963–1986) and held professorships at the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University.
